ollama_bare_import.import_method: Modelfile with only `FROM /path/to/Qwen3-14B-Q6_K.gguf`, no TEMPLATE directive
ollama_bare_import.result: GATE FAIL — 4/4 properties FAIL, all HTTP 400: 'registry.ollama.ai/library/qwen3-14b-q6k-duebot:latest does not support tools'
ollama_bare_import.root_cause: `ollama show qwen3-14b-q6k-duebot --modelfile` reveals Ollama silently generated `TEMPLATE {{ .Prompt }}` — a bare content passthrough with ZERO tool awareness — instead of using the GGUF's own embedded tool-capable Jinja chat_template (confirmed present via the same GGUF metadata parser: tokenizer.chat_template, 4100 chars, native <tool_call> XML-tag format). This is NOT a version artifact alone — Mini's newer Ollama 0.32.14 DOES correctly auto-wire tool support for its OFFICIALLY-PULLED qwen3:8b (which ships its own curated Ollama-authored Template layer from the registry, distinct from the GGUF's own embedded template). The defect is specific to the HAND-IMPORT path: `ollama create` from a bare Modelfile does not reliably promote the GGUF's own chat_template into tool-capable serving.
ollama_bare_import.significance: This is F8's own warning realized exactly: 'the serving layer must not silently turn tools into plain user text.' Ollama did not even get that far — it refused the request outright with HTTP 400 rather than silently flattening, which is a LOUDER failure than the one F8 anticipated (good, in the sense that it fails closed, not open) but still a complete round-trip failure that a naive 'just pull the GGUF into Ollama' deployment would ship with zero warning.
ollama_bare_import.file: 14b-ollama-roundtrip.json (negative-evidence artifact — kept deliberately, per orchestrator: 'a trap is only proven by the run that falls into it')

ollama_with_native_template.fix_applied: Modelfile with an explicit `TEMPLATE """..."""` — the Go-template text extracted VERBATIM from Mini's officially-pulled `qwen3:8b` Ollama-library import (blob sha256-ae370d884f108d16e7cc8fd5259ebc5773a0afa6e078b11f4ed7e39a27e0dfc4), which correctly handles .Tools / .ToolCalls / role=tool. Full text preserved as its own artifact: b4b-ollama-native-tool-template.txt.
ollama_with_native_template.authoritative_tag: qwen3-14b-q6k-duebot-tmpl (the ONLY tag kept resident/on-disk after cleanup — the bare tag's manifest was removed, its shared blob layer is unaffected since -tmpl still references it)
ollama_with_native_template.d_parallel_tool_calls_false_honored: FAIL — same shape as llama.cpp and as the 8B finding
ollama_with_native_template.context_size_caveat: IMPORTANT ASYMMETRY, flagged during the run and left in the record rather than quietly re-run: llama-server's footprint discipline (ctx=4096) does NOT carry over to Ollama automatically — Ollama sets context via a Modelfile `PARAMETER num_ctx` line, not a launch flag, and none was added here. The resident model reported CONTEXT 32768 (Ollama's own default, driven by the GGUF's context_length=40960 metadata), 15GB RSS vs llama-server's 11.59GB for the identical weights. The two stacks' round-trip/golden results are NOT footprint-equivalent experiments — this is recorded explicitly per orchestrator instruction, not smoothed over.

same_overall_rate_different_failure_set.llama_cpp_only_failure: gc-024 — llama.cpp FABRICATED a status-change mutation (new_status='rejected', reason_code='data_error') on a request that never specified a target status; Ollama correctly declined to mutate on the identical case. A real, safety-relevant cross-stack behavioral divergence on the SAME model weights, not explained by anything measured here (candidate causes: llama-server's --jinja native-template parse of the GGUF's own chat_template vs Ollama's hand-copied hand-authored Template producing a subtly different rendered prompt; not isolated further in this lane).
same_overall_rate_different_failure_set.ollama_only_failure: gc-009 — no tool call, empty content, on a case llama.cpp passed.
same_overall_rate_different_failure_set.caveat: Given the context-size asymmetry above (ctx 4096 vs 32768) and different `--reasoning off` (server flag) vs `think:false` (per-request field) mechanisms, this divergence is reported as a MEASURED finding, not attributed to 'the stack' in isolation — too many uncontrolled variables differ between the two runs to call it a clean A/B.

most_severe_individual_finding.description: Model returned tool_calls=[] (no tool call at all) but content = "The reminder for practice PR-3090 has been successfully created and is scheduled for **Thursday, August 26, 2026 at 14:00** (UTC+8). Let me know if you need further adjustments! 📅" — a fabricated SUCCESS confirmation for an action that never happened. Worse than a missed tool call: in a real WhatsApp deployment this tells staff 'done' while nothing was written to the CRM. (Also internally wrong on its own terms: 2026-08-26 is a Wednesday per the case's own consistent weekday math, not Thursday — the hallucination is not even self-consistent.)

other_findings.pattern: Staff-name-to-ID resolution with no lookup tool available (gc-008, gc-021)
other_findings.llama_cpp_behavior: Fabricates a plausible-looking but FAKE user_id ('USR-00123') — same fake ID both times, suggesting a memorized placeholder pattern rather than random hallucination. This is the more dangerous failure mode: 'USR-00123' matches the ^USR-[0-9]{3,8}$ schema pattern and could silently misassign to a real-but-wrong staff member if one happens to hold that ID.
other_findings.ollama_behavior: Passes the raw name through verbatim ('Asya', 'Ari') instead of an ID. Also wrong (violates 'never invent IDs' is moot since it's not invented, but violates the ID-not-name contract), but fails LOUDER — a downstream schema validator (`^USR-[0-9]{3,8}$`) would reject 'Asya' immediately, where 'USR-00123' would pass syntactic validation and fail only if checked against a real roster.
other_findings.scope_caveat: assigned_to is documented as optional, defaulting server-side to the requesting staff member if omitted — the objectively SAFEST model behavior when it cannot resolve a name (no list_assignable_staff tool was in this 5-tool subset) is to OMIT the field, which neither stack did. This is disclosed as a real, if partially scope-limited (missing lookup tool), defect: the system prompt's own 'never invent IDs' / 'use a read-only lookup t001 first' rule does not fall back to 'omit the optional field' when no lookup tool exists for the entity in question.

other_findings.llama_cpp_behavior: Fabricated practice_id='PR-12345' (matches no real world-fact ID) AND called the wrong tool (mark_document_received directly, skipping search_clients) for 'KTP-nya Siti Rahayu udah diterima' — a direct violation of the explicit system-prompt rule 'If an ID is missing, use a read-only lookup tool first.'
other_findings.significance: The single most safety-relevant llama.cpp-specific finding: an R2 mutation call with a wholly invented, syntactically-valid ID.

other_findings.pattern: Multi-turn correction not applied (gc-015 llama.cpp variant, gc-018 both stacks)
other_findings.description: When a user corrects an earlier relative-date resolution mid-conversation ('eh maaf, maksudku hari Kamis ya' / confirms a stated Friday date then executes with Thursday's date instead), both stacks sometimes execute with the PRE-correction or an off-by-one-day value rather than the corrected/confirmed one. On gc-018 specifically, the model's own PRIOR turn correctly states 'venerdì 28/08/2026' in a confirmation question, then the SAME model executes the tool call with 27/08 (its own confirmation didn't survive to execution) — an internal self-consistency failure, not just a date-math error.

footprint_discipline_applied: np=1/ctx=4096 for llama-server (vs the generic np=4/ctx=8192 reference) — sequential inference only was needed for gate runs.
Never two large models resident concurrently across BOTH machines and BOTH stacks at any point (verified via ps/pgrep/ollama ps before and after every load/unload transition).

GAP, disclosed not hidden: the ctx=4096 discipline did not carry over to the Ollama runs (Ollama sets context via Modelfile PARAMETER num_ctx, not a launch flag; none was added) — Ollama ran at its own default (32768). This is recorded as an asymmetry between the two stacks' experiments, not smoothed over.

All large-model processes (llama-server, ollama-loaded model) killed/unloaded and verified gone (process check + port-refused / ollama ps empty) before every stack transition and at the end of the lane.

Cleanup executed immediately after the last gate run completed, per orchestrator instruction, not deferred to end-of-lane — final df -h/vm_stat taken AFTER cleanup so the recorded numbers are true at report time.
open_items_for_the_orchestrator: F8's Mini-production-capacity assumption (Qwen3-14B Q6_K resident alongside Postgres/Redis/cron) is UNMEASURED — both memory readings taken tonight were under non-steady-state multi-session load. Needs a dedicated steady-state measurement before being treated as settled in either direction.

The gc-024 cross-stack behavioral divergence (llama.cpp fabricated a mutation on an ambiguous case; Ollama correctly declined) is measured but not root-caused — too many confounds (context size, thinking-disable mechanism, template rendering differences) differ between the two runs to isolate the cause here.

assigned_to (staff-name resolution) failures are partially attributable to the 5-tool subset excluding list_assignable_staff — worth re-testing with the full 10-tool F5 registry before this specific failure mode is treated as fully characterized.

The Ollama hand-import tool-blindness trap (bare Modelfile -> silent TEMPLATE {{ .Prompt }} fallback) is a NEW, previously-unmeasured finding with implications beyond this lane — any future Ollama deployment of a model NOT already curated in the Ollama library needs an explicit tool-aware TEMPLATE, verified empirically, not assumed from the GGUF's own embedded chat_template.
